title: A two-way adapter between Enumeration and Iterator

blocks.text: The page's Q4 lists adapters in the JDK itself: `Collections.enumeration` adapts a collection to the legacy `Enumeration`, and `Collections.list` adapts an `Enumeration` back. Write the same bridge between the two iteration interfaces yourself, in both directions (the page's two-way adapter idea):

items: `asEnumeration(iterator)` returns an `Enumeration<T>` the other way round.

blocks.text: Like `Arrays.asList`, each result is **a view that reads the source only when asked**: nothing is copied up front, and each `next()` takes one element. **Past the end, both throw `NoSuchElementException`**, as their interfaces require.

cases.says: asIterator walks an Enumeration's elements in order, and asEnumeration walks an Iterator's elements in order.
Creating the iterator and calling hasNext() takes no element from the Enumeration; each next() takes exactly one.
next() after the last element throws NoSuchElementException, and so does nextElement() on the adapted Enumeration.

concepts: The JDK has adapters of its own, such as Arrays.asList as a view of an array and Collections.enumeration and Collections.list between collections and Enumeration.
A two-way adapter lets each of two interfaces be used where the other is expected.
